finding.claim: OS command injection in /ping: the unauthenticated `host` query parameter is concatenated directly into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, so shell metacharacters (; | && $() backticks) execute arbitrary commands as the server user. Command output is also returned in the response, giving the attacker direct feedback.
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, which spawns /bin/sh -c

trace.note: Express route handler for GET /ping, no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated into shell command string and passed to exec()
stdout returned to the client, so injected command output is exfiltrated

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist, or hostname/IP regex; no authentication or authorization middleware; no use of execFile/argument array; no escaping. req.query.host can also be an array or object (e.g. ?host[]=a), but string concatenation still reaches the shell. Example payload: /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id. The app listens on 3001 with no host binding restriction.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (a shell) with no auth middleware, validation or escaping anywhere in the file (app.use is never called), and tools.js:11 returns stdout on success, so `;id` injection works. Only the success output is returned (errors give an empty 502), but commands that exit 0 still leak their output.

verdict_facts.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (a shell) with no auth, validation or escaping, and tools.js:11 returns stdout to the client. The /ping route is anonymous and tools.js is the only file in the directory. With `127.0.0.1;id` the shell exits 0 because `id` is the last command, so the output is sent rather than the 502 at line 9.
